headline: High: shared web-app/MCP and broad network egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui explicitly supports MCP, plugins, tools, and OpenAPI servers, while kotaemon ingests documents/HTML and uses a web UI with broad egress. That creates a plausible default pathway where attacker-controlled content from A can be fed into B’s tool-using interface and interpreted as instructions. The interaction is documented by profiles, though not sandboxed.
conditions: IF kotaemon content is copied into open-webui chats or tools without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF open-webui MCP or plugin outputs are treated as instructions, attacker text from kotaemon can steer actions.
mitigations: Disable MCP/plugins for the shared workflow.
Add a manual provenance check before pasting A outputs into B.
Use a read-only export format for A outputs.
Restrict B tool use to allowlisted commands.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch API keys and files, and both have broad network egress. kotaemon stores data under ./ktem_app_data and handles secrets; open-webui uses local files/mounted volumes plus persistent sessions and external APIs. If they share a workspace or operator account, sensitive documents or keys can flow from one agent into the other and then out to third-party services.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or mounted volume, file leakage is possible.
IF either agent sends loaded context to external APIs, secrets or documents can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate storage directories for each agent.
Remove secrets from shared files before use.
Turn on offline mode where possible.
Rotate any API keys exposed to either agent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and broad network egress, and open-webui adds persistent shared sessions plus Redis-backed state. kotaemon also writes to ./ktem_app_data. Even without explicit same-dir evidence, overlapping mutable state and concurrent instances make write conflicts plausible; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same mounted directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF open-webui sessions and kotaemon state are shared across workers, concurrent updates can race.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent writes during shared tasks.
Serialize edits with a simple operator checklist.
Back up shared files before running both agents.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui is a tool-using orchestrator, and kotaemon produces documents, citations, and chat transcripts that can be treated as authoritative inputs. If B consumes A’s outputs without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream tool actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default web-app workflows, so uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF open-webui forwards kotaemon outputs into tools or agents without verification, cascading errors can trigger actions.
IF kotaemon-generated citations are accepted as ground truth, downstream decisions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before tool execution.
Cross-check citations against source documents.
Limit B to read-only actions for shared tasks.
Flag low-confidence outputs from A.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between A and B.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles show broad handling of documents and API keys, but only open-webui explicitly exposes persistent sessions, analytics, and multiple external services. No direct residency or certification mismatch is documented, so this is a policy-gap risk rather than a proven breach. The evidence is insufficient for high severity, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through open-webui’s external services, retention or residency obligations may be violated.
IF kotaemon and open-webui are used on the same sensitive corpus, policy mismatches can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of external APIs.
Review retention settings in both tools.
Disable analytics where possible.
Use separate datasets for regulated and non-regulated work.
requires-engineering: document and enforce a data-processing agreement and residency policy.
